meta.title: Projects & case studies
meta.description: A closer look at selected solar, electrical, drywall, masonry and roofing projects — what we set out to do, how we approached it, and the result.

index.title: Projects & case studies
index.subtitle: A closer look at how we plan and deliver work across our five trades.

solarFarm.title: Rooftop photovoltaic power plant
solarFarm.summary: Design and installation of a rooftop PV system for an industrial building, including project documentation and connection to the distribution grid.
solarFarm.overview: A grid-connected photovoltaic system across the roof of a large industrial building, sized to cover a meaningful share of the site's daytime electricity demand. We carried the project from initial feasibility through documentation, installation and energisation.
solarFarm.challenge: The roof had to carry a full array without compromising its waterproofing or structure, and the connection to the distribution grid required the network operator's approval before the plant could be switched on.
scope: Mounting structures, panels, inverters and protection
Commissioning, grid connection and monitoring handover

process.title: Survey & feasibility
process.body: We assessed the roof's structure, orientation and shading, then modelled the expected yield to size the array realistically.

process.title: Documentation & approvals
process.body: We prepared the project documentation and handled the grid-connection application with the distribution operator.

process.title: Installation
process.body: Mounting structures, panels, inverters and protection were installed with the existing roof membrane kept intact throughout.

process.title: Commissioning
process.body: The system was tested, connected to the grid and handed over with monitoring so output can be tracked over time.

solarFarm.outcome: The building now generates a substantial share of its own electricity during daylight hours, with remote monitoring in place to confirm performance season to season.

groundMountSolar.title: Ground-mounted solar park with storage
groundMountSolar.summary: Turnkey ground-mounted PV array of approximately 480 kWp paired with battery storage, delivered from foundations through to grid connection.
groundMountSolar.overview: A turnkey ground-mounted solar park of roughly 480 kWp on a former brownfield plot, paired with battery storage so generation can be shifted toward evening peak demand. We delivered the whole chain, from groundworks to energisation.
groundMountSolar.challenge: A sloping, previously disturbed site meant the mounting structures had to be set out precisely, and adding storage required the inverter and protection design to handle both charge and discharge cleanly.
scope: Site setting-out, foundations and mounting structures

process.title: Groundworks
process.body: We set out the rows to the terrain and installed foundations and mounting structures suited to the recovered ground.

process.title: Array & storage
process.body: Panels, inverters and the battery system were installed and wired so storage charges from surplus generation.

process.title: Grid connection
process.body: Protection, metering and the connection to the network were completed in line with the operator's requirements.

process.title: Commissioning
process.body: We tested generation and storage together and handed the plant over with monitoring of both.

groundMountSolar.outcome: The plant covers daytime demand and uses stored energy to reduce evening peaks, commissioned and handed over within a single construction season.

retailWiring.title: Electrical fit-out for retail premises
retailWiring.summary: High- and low-voltage wiring including LED lighting, distribution boards and an intruder alarm for commercial premises.
retailWiring.overview: A complete electrical fit-out of retail premises, covering power, lighting and low-voltage systems from the distribution boards to the final fittings. The work was sequenced around the tenant's fit-out so the space could open on schedule.
retailWiring.challenge: Power and low-voltage systems had to be coordinated with the shopfitters and finishes, and the alarm and lighting needed to be commissioned and certified before opening.

process.title: Coordination
process.body: We set the routes and board positions with the shopfitters so first-fix could run ahead of the finishes.

process.title: First fix
process.body: Containment, cabling and back-boxes were installed before walls and ceilings were closed up.

process.title: Second fix
process.body: Boards, luminaires, accessories and the alarm were fitted and connected.

process.title: Testing & handover
process.body: Circuits were tested and certified, the alarm commissioned, and the installation handed over for opening.

retailWiring.outcome: The premises opened on time with a fully tested and certified electrical installation, energy-efficient LED lighting and a working intruder alarm.

evChargingHub.title: EV charging hub for a logistics depot
evChargingHub.summary: DC fast-charging bays for a commercial vehicle fleet, load-managed to stay within the site's available grid capacity.
evChargingHub.overview: An electric-vehicle charging hub for a commercial fleet, built around fast-charging bays fed from an upgraded supply and load-managed so the site never exceeds its available grid capacity.
evChargingHub.challenge: Charging a fleet at once would have overloaded the existing connection, so the design had to combine a supply upgrade with active load management rather than simply adding chargers.
scope: Supply upgrade from the transformer station
Fast chargers with dynamic load management

process.title: Capacity assessment
process.body: We measured the available supply and planned an upgrade plus load management to cover simultaneous charging.

process.title: Civils & cabling
process.body: Trenching, ducting and cable runs were installed from the upgraded supply to each bay.

process.title: Chargers
process.body: Fast chargers were mounted, connected and configured for dynamic load sharing across the bays.

process.title: Integration & commissioning
process.body: Chargers were linked to the operator's billing and monitoring system, then tested under load.

evChargingHub.outcome: The depot can charge multiple vehicles at once without breaching its connection limit, with usage and billing visible through the operator's platform.

warehousePower.title: Warehouse power and LED high-bay lighting
warehousePower.summary: Low-voltage distribution and LED high-bay lighting for a 9,000 m² logistics warehouse, controlled by daylight and presence sensors.
warehousePower.overview: A combined power and lighting fit-out for a 9,000 m² logistics warehouse: low-voltage distribution laid out around the racking, and LED high-bay lighting controlled by daylight and presence sensors.
warehousePower.challenge: The lighting had to suit tall racking aisles and a working floor, while the retrofit of older fittings needed to happen with minimal disruption to ongoing operations.
scope: LED high-bay lighting designed to the aisle layout

process.title: Lighting design
process.body: We designed the high-bay layout around the racking aisles and the working floor to give even, usable light levels.

process.title: Power distribution
process.body: Low-voltage distribution and final circuits were installed to feed lighting and equipment.

process.title: Controls
process.body: Daylight and presence sensors were set up so lighting dims or switches with conditions and occupancy.

process.title: Changeover
process.body: Legacy fittings were removed and the installation tested, certified and handed over with minimal downtime.

warehousePower.outcome: The warehouse runs on efficient, well-controlled lighting that responds to daylight and occupancy, with noticeably lower lighting energy use and better light on the picking floor.

officeFitout.title: Office drywall fit-out
officeFitout.summary: Complete drywall partitions, suspended ceilings and acoustic solutions for a newly refurbished office space.
officeFitout.overview: A full drywall fit-out of a refurbished office floor — partitions, suspended ceilings and acoustic treatment — delivered to the architect's layout and finish schedule.
officeFitout.challenge: Open-plan and meeting spaces needed sensible acoustic separation, and the ceilings had to coordinate cleanly with lighting, ventilation and sprinklers.
scope: Metal-stud partitions to the office layout
Jointing and finishing ready for decoration

process.title: Set-out
process.body: We set out partitions and ceiling grids to the architect's drawings and the services layout.

process.title: Framing
process.body: Metal-stud framing went up with acoustic insulation where separation between spaces was needed.

process.title: Boarding & ceilings
process.body: Partitions were boarded and suspended ceilings installed, coordinated with lighting and ventilation.

process.title: Finishing
process.body: Joints were taped and filled and surfaces left ready for decoration.

officeFitout.outcome: The floor was handed over ready for decoration, with clean lines, well-judged acoustics and ceilings that integrate the building services tidily.

clinicFitout.title: Outpatient clinic interior fit-out
clinicFitout.summary: Fire-rated and hygienic drywall partitions, suspended ceilings and acoustic treatment for an outpatient clinic across two floors.
clinicFitout.overview: An interior drywall fit-out for an outpatient clinic over two floors, built to healthcare standards: fire-rated and hygienic partitions, suspended ceilings and acoustic treatment around consulting and procedure rooms.
clinicFitout.challenge: Healthcare interiors demand cleanable, fire-rated and in places radiation-shielded construction, all while holding tight tolerances around medical services and ductwork.
scope: Fire-rated partitions to consulting and procedure rooms
Hygienic, cleanable wall junctions and finishes
Lead-lined walls to the imaging room
Coordination with medical services and ventilation

process.title: Compliance set-out
process.body: We set out partitions to the fire, hygiene and shielding requirements of each room.

process.title: Specialist framing
process.body: Framing and boarding included lead lining to the imaging room and detailing for cleanable junctions.

process.title: Ceilings & services
process.body: Suspended ceilings were installed to tight tolerances around medical services and ductwork.

process.title: Finishing
process.body: Surfaces were finished to a hygienic, easily cleaned standard ready for the clinic's fit-out.

clinicFitout.outcome: The clinic took over interiors that meet healthcare requirements for fire, hygiene and shielding, with ceilings and finishes that sit cleanly around the medical services.

apartmentReroof.title: Apartment block pitched-roof renewal
apartmentReroof.summary: Full renewal of a five-storey block's pitched roof — battens, membrane, clay tiles, insulation and tinwork — carried out in phases with the building occupied.
apartmentReroof.overview: A complete renewal of the pitched roof on a five-storey residential block — new battens, membrane, clay tiles, insulation and tinwork — carried out in phases so residents could stay in their homes throughout.
apartmentReroof.challenge: Working over an occupied building meant strict attention to weather protection and safety, with each phase made watertight before the next was opened up.
scope: Strip-out of the existing roof covering

process.title: Phasing & protection
process.body: We split the roof into sections so each could be opened, worked and made watertight without exposing the flats below.

process.title: Strip & build-up
process.body: The old covering came off and new insulation, membrane and battens went on, section by section.

process.title: Tiling & detailing
process.body: Clay tiles were laid and dormers, penetrations and flashings detailed for a weathertight finish.

process.title: Rainwater & handover
process.body: The rainwater system was renewed and the completed roof handed over.

apartmentReroof.outcome: The block has a renewed, properly insulated and weathertight roof, delivered in phases that kept residents in place throughout the works.

retainingWall.title: Reinforced retaining wall and site masonry
retainingWall.summary: Reinforced retaining structure stabilising a sloped plot for a new-build house, with natural-stone facing, drainage and landscaping masonry.
retainingWall.overview: A reinforced retaining structure to stabilise a sloped plot for a new-build house, finished with natural-stone facing and tied into steps and landscaping walls across the grounds.
retainingWall.challenge: The slope and groundwater had to be controlled to secure the terrain above, while the visible faces needed a natural-stone finish in keeping with the house.
scope: Excavation and foundations to the slope

process.title: Groundworks
process.body: We excavated and formed foundations sized to the slope and the loads above.

process.title: Structure
process.body: The reinforced retaining structure was built and backed with drainage to manage groundwater.

process.title: Facing
process.body: Natural-stone facing was laid to give the visible faces a finish that suits the house.

process.title: Landscaping
process.body: Steps and lower landscaping walls were tied in to complete the grounds.

retainingWall.outcome: The terrain above is secured against movement and water, with natural-stone faces and integrated steps that finish the grounds neatly.

industrialRoof.title: Industrial hall re-roofing
industrialRoof.summary: Strip and replacement of an existing flat roof with a membrane waterproofing system on a manufacturing facility.
industrialRoof.overview: A re-roofing of a manufacturing hall, replacing a worn flat roof with a new membrane waterproofing system over the working facility. The project is currently underway.
industrialRoof.challenge: The hall stays in production during the works, so the roof has to be stripped and re-covered in sections that are made watertight each day without interrupting the operation below.
scope: Phased strip-out of the existing flat roof

process.title: Survey & plan
process.body: We surveyed the existing roof and planned a phased build-up that keeps the hall watertight day to day.

process.title: Phased strip-out
process.body: The worn covering is being removed in sections sized to be re-covered within each working window.

process.title: New waterproofing
process.body: Insulation and a new membrane system are being laid, with flashings and outlets renewed.

process.title: Drainage & completion
process.body: Roof drainage is being brought up to standard as each section is closed in.

industrialRoof.outcome: Work is progressing section by section, keeping the facility in production while the roof is replaced; completion and handover are scheduled within the current programme.

brickFacade.title: Brick facade and masonry work
brickFacade.summary: Load-bearing masonry and a clay-brick facade for a multi-unit residential building, including lintels and openings.
brickFacade.overview: Load-bearing masonry and a clay-brick facade for a multi-unit residential building, including lintels and openings. The structure and facade are being built in step with the wider project.
brickFacade.challenge: The facade has to read as a clean, regular brick pattern while the masonry behind it carries load and frames the window and door openings accurately.
scope: Load-bearing masonry to the structural design
Setting-out of window and door openings

process.title: Set-out
process.body: We set out the walls and openings from the structural drawings so the facade pattern stays regular.

process.title: Load-bearing masonry
process.body: The structural masonry is being built with lintels placed over the openings as the walls rise.

process.title: Brick facade
process.body: The clay-brick facade is being laid to a consistent bond and joint across the elevations.

process.title: Detailing
process.body: Movement joints and opening details are being completed as each elevation is finished.

brickFacade.outcome: The masonry and facade are going up in step with the build; the elevations completed so far show the clean, regular brickwork the design calls for.

solarCarport.title: Solar carport with EV charging
solarCarport.summary: Planned photovoltaic carport structure with integrated electric-vehicle charging points for a corporate car park.
solarCarport.overview: A planned photovoltaic carport for a corporate car park: a canopy structure carrying solar panels, with electric-vehicle charging points integrated beneath it. The project is in planning.
solarCarport.challenge: The structure needs to shade and shelter parking while carrying the array, and the charging points have to be fed and load-managed within the site's electrical capacity.

process.title: Concept & layout
process.body: We will set the canopy layout to the parking bays and size the array and chargers to the site.

process.title: Structure
process.body: The carport structure will be built to carry the array and shelter the parking below.

process.title: PV & charging
process.body: Panels and EV charging points will be installed, fed and load-managed within capacity.

process.title: Connection
process.body: The system will be connected, commissioned and handed over with monitoring.

solarCarport.outcome: Once built, the carport will shelter parking, generate solar power and charge vehicles from a single structure — combining our solar and electrical work in one place.

meta.title: Quantum Sphere — Turnkey construction works | Slovakia
meta.description: Comprehensive construction services across five trades: solar power plants, electrical installations, drywall, masonry and roof installation.

hero.title: Complete construction solutions under one roof
hero.subtitle: We cover the full range of trades, from solar power plants to roofing. One company, five trades, one accountable partner.

about.title: About Quantum Sphere
about.body: We are a construction company based in Slovakia. We specialise in comprehensive delivery across five trades. We work for both business and private clients, and thanks to our own teams in every trade we can carry out most projects without subcontractors.

values.title: Why Quantum Sphere
values.subtitle: Four reasons our clients trust us with their projects

items.title: Experienced in-house teams
items.body: Every trade is delivered by our own staff — no random subcontractors. That gives us full control over quality and schedule.

items.title: Quality and safety
items.body: We work to applicable standards and occupational-safety regulations. Every project is handed over with the relevant documentation and inspection reports.

items.title: Reliable deadlines
items.body: We treat the agreed schedule as a commitment. We keep clients regularly informed and deal with any complications early.

items.title: Full-service delivery
items.body: From solar power plants to roofing — everything under one roof. One partner for five trades means simpler coordination and fewer headaches for you.

coverage.title: Where we work
coverage.body: We carry out projects across Slovakia, with our base in Bratislava. Selected larger commissions are also delivered for clients in Central Europe and the wider EU — reflected in our five-language support.

featuredProjects.subtitle: A sample of projects from recent years

solar.name: Solar power plants
solar.tagline: Turnkey design and installation of PV systems

meta.title: Turnkey solar power plants | Quantum Sphere
meta.description: Design, supply and installation of photovoltaic systems. Rooftop and ground-mount installations for businesses, municipalities and homes.

hero.title: Photovoltaic systems for businesses and homes
hero.subtitle: From design and project documentation through mounting panels, inverters and batteries to connection to the distribution grid.

solar.description: We deliver photovoltaic power plants for building roofs, ground-mount installations and agri-PV. We work with proven components and manage the whole process with our own team — from the site survey to operational monitoring.

deliverables.title: What we provide
items: Site survey, system design and optimisation
Supply of PV panels, inverters and mounting structures
Monitoring setup and handover to the client

steps.title: Free site survey
steps.body: We assess the roof structure, orientation and shading. We measure consumption and propose the optimal capacity.

steps.title: Quote and contract
steps.body: We present a transparent calculation including subsidies and financing. Once approved, we sign a works contract.

steps.title: Project documentation
steps.body: We prepare the implementation project and arrange all the necessary approvals from the distribution company.

steps.title: Installation and connection
steps.body: Installation usually takes 2–5 days depending on size. Our team handles the installation, wiring and inspection.

steps.title: Handover and service
steps.body: After grid connection and monitoring setup we hand over the work with documentation. We provide a warranty and post-warranty service.

certifications.title: Certificates and qualifications
items: Electrician competence for PV work (per Slovak Decree 508/2009)

items.q: How long until a solar investment pays back?
items.a: At current electricity prices and with appropriate sizing, payback in Slovakia is most often 6–9 years. We prepare a specific calculation after the site survey.

For family homes, batteries pay off if you generate more than you consume in summer and want to use the surplus in the evening. For businesses with daytime consumption, a PV system without batteries is often more efficient.
Yes. We can guide you through applying for the currently available subsidies. We prepare the documents and can handle communication with the authorities.

electrical.name: Electrical installations

meta.title: Electrical installations for businesses and sites | Quantum Sphere
meta.description: Complete high- and low-voltage electrical installations for new builds, renovations and industrial buildings.

hero.title: Electrical installations to standard
hero.subtitle: We deliver high- and low-voltage wiring, distribution boards and intelligent controls for commercial and residential projects.

electrical.description: We cover the entire electrical part of a construction project — from laying cables during the shell stage through fitting distribution boards to inspections and handover. We work with a certified inspection technician and all installations comply with the applicable standards.

deliverables.title: What we provide
items: Low-voltage systems (data, intruder alarm, fire alarm, CCTV)

steps.title: Consultation and survey
steps.body: We go through the construction drawings with you, identify needs and propose the optimal layout.

steps.title: Quote
steps.body: We prepare a detailed itemised budget with a clear material specification.

steps.title: First-fix installation
steps.body: Laying cables, boxes and conduits before plastering. Coordination with the other trades.

steps.title: Final installation
steps.body: Fitting sockets, switches, light fittings, distribution boards and end devices.

steps.title: Inspection and handover
steps.body: Initial professional inspection and test, issuing the inspection report and handing over the work.

items.q: Do you carry out inspections without doing the installation?
items.a: Yes, we provide initial and periodic professional inspections and tests for buildings we did not construct.

items.q: What is the difference between high and low voltage?
items.a: High voltage is the usual 230/400 V wiring for appliances and lighting. Low voltage covers data, telephone, camera, security and fire systems with voltages up to 50 V.

drywall.name: Drywall

meta.title: Drywall works | Quantum Sphere
meta.description: Drywall partitions, suspended ceilings, acoustic and fire-rated systems for offices, flats and commercial spaces.

hero.title: Drywall for offices, flats and industry
hero.subtitle: Partitions, ceilings, lining walls and special structures — with attention to acoustics, fire resistance and the quality of the details.

drywall.description: We build drywall structures of all kinds — from simple partitions to multi-layer acoustic and fire-rated systems. We work with Knauf and Rigips systems according to the manufacturer's system rules.

steps.title: Measuring
steps.body: Precise measuring of the space and defining the technical parameters (acoustics, fire).

steps.title: Framework
steps.body: Installing the steel substructure according to the system rules.

steps.title: Boarding
steps.body: Installing the plasterboard, including insulation and service cavities.

steps.title: Jointing and sanding
steps.body: Filling the joints and screw heads, sanding smooth ready for painting.

certifications.title: System certifications
items: Fire-rated assemblies EI per STN EN 13501

items.q: What is the fire resistance of drywall partitions?
items.a: Depending on the specific build-up, from EI 15 to EI 90. We design the specific build-up to the requirements of the project.

masonry.name: Masonry

meta.title: Masonry works | Quantum Sphere
meta.description: Structural and finishing masonry for new builds and renovations. Bricklaying, plastering, concreting, tiling and paving.

hero.title: Masonry for new builds and renovations
hero.subtitle: We cover the full range of the masonry trade, from foundations to final plaster and tiling.

masonry.description: We carry out masonry work to a quality that matches modern building demands. We work with reputable suppliers of building materials and all work is done by our own stable team.

deliverables.title: What we provide
items: Bricklaying of external and internal walls

steps.title: Survey and costing
steps.body: We assess the scope, propose the approach and prepare a quote.

steps.title: Site preparation
steps.body: Securing materials and protecting adjacent surfaces.

steps.title: Execution
steps.body: Work to the agreed schedule with ongoing quality control.

steps.title: Handover
steps.body: Cleaning the site, handing over the work and invoicing.

certifications.title: Standards and practices
items: Construction waste management per applicable regulations

items.q: Do you also do smaller renovations?
items.a: Yes. We carry out renovations of bathroom cores, bathrooms and smaller masonry alterations.

roofing.name: Roof installation

meta.title: Roof installation | Quantum Sphere
meta.description: Complete roof deliveries — pitched roofs with clay or metal tiles, flat roofs with membrane waterproofing, sheet-metal work.

hero.title: Roofs with attention to detail
hero.subtitle: Pitched roofs, flat roofs, re-covering and sheet-metal work. We work with Bramac, Tondach, Lindab and Sarnafil systems.

roofing.description: We build roofs for new buildings and renovations. On every roof we focus on the correct build-up, ventilation and quality sheet-metal details, which determine the lifespan of the work.

deliverables.title: What we provide
items: Pitched roofs with clay or concrete tiles

steps.title: Roof survey
steps.body: We assess the condition of the structure and covering and propose the optimal solution.

steps.title: Design and quote
steps.body: A detailed budget with the specific roof build-up.

steps.title: Stripping the old covering
steps.body: For renovations, safe removal and disposal of the old covering.

steps.title: Laying the new build-up
steps.body: Breathable membrane, counter-battens, battens, covering and sheet-metal details.

steps.title: Warranty
steps.body: A 5-year warranty on the work; on materials according to the manufacturer.

certifications.title: System training and standards
items: Lindab — certified partner for metal roof systems

items.q: What is the lifespan of clay tiles?
items.a: With quality installation and maintenance, 60–100 years. Sheet-metal elements have a shorter lifespan (20–40 years), so we account for them separately.

items.q: When is a flat roof more suitable?
items.a: Flat roofs suit office and industrial buildings where the roof is used, for example for photovoltaics. For a family home it depends on the architectural concept.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy

controller.heading: 1. Controller
controller.body:

Quantum Sphere s.r.o.

scope.heading: 2. Data we process
scope.body:
We process only the data you provide to us via the contact form or by email:

• Full name
• Email address
• Phone number (optional)
• Company name (optional)
• Type of service you are interested in
• Content of your message

When you visit the website we process technical data (IP address, browser type, time of visit) to the extent necessary for the secure operation of the service.

purpose.heading: 3. Purpose and legal basis
purpose.body:
We process data from the contact form for the following purposes:

• Handling your enquiry and communicating about it — legal basis: Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (pre-contractual relations and performance of a contract).
• Keeping records of business correspondence — legal basis: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interest of the controller).
• Technical logs of website visits (IP address, user agent, time) — legal basis: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interest in secure and protected service operation).

Marketing cookies (analytics) are processed exclusively on the basis of your explicit consent — Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR — given via the cookie banner. You may withdraw consent at any time.

retention.heading: 4. Retention periods
retention.body:
Data from the contact form is retained for the duration of processing your enquiry and thereafter for a maximum of 3 years from the last contact (legitimate interest — correspondence records). If a business relationship is established, this period is extended in accordance with statutory time limits (in particular accounting and tax regulations).

Technical logs of website visits are retained for a maximum of 30 days.

recipients.heading: 5. Recipients and processors
recipients.body:
Your data is disclosed only to the following categories of recipients, to the extent necessary for the purpose:

• Vercel Inc. (USA) — website hosting and delivery infrastructure. Transfer of data to the USA is secured by Standard Contractual Clauses (SCC) pursuant to Art. 46 GDPR.
• Supabase (EU) — database storage of form messages.
• SMTP provider (Slovakia/EU) — delivery of email notification of a new enquiry.
• PostHog Inc. (USA) — anonymised website analytics, exclusively if you give consent. Transfer to the USA covered by SCC.

We do not sell or provide your data to third parties for marketing purposes.

rights.heading: 6. Your rights
rights.body:
Under the GDPR you have the right:

• to access your data (Art. 15),
• to rectification of inaccurate data (Art. 16),
• to erasure of data (Art. 17), where it is no longer necessary for the purpose for which it was collected,
• to restriction of processing (Art. 18),
• to data portability (Art. 20),
• to object to processing based on legitimate interest (Art. 21),
• to withdraw consent to analytics cookies at any time (Art. 7(3)) — withdrawal has no retroactive effect.

services.heading: 2. Scope of Services
services.body: The Contractor provides construction and installation services across five trades: solar power plant installation, electrical installations, drywall work, masonry, and roof installation. Quotations are non-binding and valid for 30 days from the date of issue unless otherwise stated. A quotation becomes binding only upon written confirmation of the order by both parties.

contract.heading: 3. Formation of Contract
contract.body: A contract is formed upon the Contractor's written confirmation of the order or upon signature of a separate works contract. Confirmation by e-mail is considered written. Any changes to the scope of work must be agreed in writing and may affect the price and completion date.

pricing.heading: 4. Prices and Payment Terms
pricing.body:
Prices are quoted exclusive of VAT unless expressly stated otherwise. VAT will be added at the statutory rate applicable on the date of the taxable supply.

Specific payment terms (due date, any deposit and method of payment) are agreed individually for each project and set out in the quotation or works contract.

In the event of late payment, the Contractor is entitled to charge statutory interest on arrears.

warranty.heading: 5. Warranty and Liability
warranty.body:
The Contractor warrants the completed work in accordance with the mandatory provisions of Slovak law. The warranty period for construction work is 24 months from the date of handover and acceptance, unless a longer period is agreed in the contract.

The Contractor's liability for damages is limited to the contract price of the work, except in cases of intentional misconduct or gross negligence. The Contractor is not liable for damage caused by force majeure.

withdrawal.heading: 6. Right of Withdrawal
withdrawal.body:
A consumer has the right to withdraw from a contract concluded at a distance or off-premises within 14 days without giving reasons, in accordance with Act No. 102/2014 Coll. The right of withdrawal does not apply where work has commenced at the consumer's express request before the withdrawal period has expired and the consumer has been duly informed of this.

The consumer right of withdrawal does not apply to contracts concluded between businesses. The parties may withdraw from the contract on grounds established by the applicable provisions of the Commercial Code or agreed in the contract.

governing.heading: 7. Governing Law and Disputes

cookies.title: Cookies

intro.heading: What are cookies
intro.body: Cookies are small text files that a website stores in your browser. They are used to make the website work (for example, remembering your language preference) or to measure traffic.

necessary.heading: Strictly necessary cookies
necessary.body:
These cookies are required for the basic functioning of the website and do not require your consent:

• NEXT_LOCALE — stores your chosen language (validity 1 year).
• authjs.session-token / authjs.csrf-token — client portal login (valid for the duration of the session).

Without these cookies the website will not function correctly.

analytics.heading: Analytics cookies (with consent)
analytics.body:
If you give consent, we store PostHog cookies for anonymised measurement of website traffic (number of visits, most-visited pages, traffic sources). Data is aggregated and is not used for profiling or advertising.

• ph_phc_* — visit identifier and PostHog SDK state (validity up to 1 year).
• Processor: PostHog Inc., USA — transfer covered by Standard Contractual Clauses.

You may withdraw consent at any time — click the “Manage cookies” link in the footer or delete cookies in your browser.

manage.heading: How to manage consent
manage.body:
When you first visit the website we will show you a cookie banner. There you can accept or decline analytics cookies. We remember your decision via the cookie "qs_consent" (validity 6 months).

You can change your consent at any time — either via the button below or by deleting cookies in your browser.

thirdParty.heading: Third-party cookies
thirdParty.body: The website does not use advertising cookies, social-network cookies, or third-party trackers beyond the PostHog instance described above.
